post.summary: Ingest, read, or compile context briefs
post.description:
Save and reuse evidence in an authorized Recoup workspace. **Preview: this reference is verified against API source, not a completed hosted acceptance test.** Actions require the corresponding database and workflow release; verification actions also require their feature to be enabled. Do not infer provider readiness, complete coverage, or a successful workflow from an accepted request schema.

### Create context

`ingest` creates or reuses a Spotify-track request and dispatches its durable workflow (202). The parser recognizes YouTube URLs, but ingestion still rejects them in this pilot. `ingest_release` stores a Spotify album locator; it does not automatically verify the release. `ingest_catalog` and `ingest_artist` refer to accessible Recoup records. `ingest_songwriter_name`, `ingest_company_name`, `ingest_campaign_brief`, and `ingest_supporting_text` store submitted context (200). Names and customer text are not verified identities or facts. Reuse an idempotency key only for the same intended input.

### Read, plan and inspect

`read` reads one request. For saved supporting text, HTTP and standard MCP also return a metadata-only `material_evidence` receipt identifying the current document, result and exact retained source version. It returns no submitted text, source location or signed access. `draft_origin` remains `not_recorded`: a retained customer assertion is not proof of its file origin or reviewed business facts. Unavailable material withholds those references. Delegated OAuth keeps its request-only response. `plan` plans modules from stored context; a plan is not authorization to collect data. `list_executions` and `read_execution` expose execution records. `list_catalog_members` pages saved members; `expand_catalog_members` materializes a bounded member page. These operations return 200. Request IDs, subject IDs and execution IDs refer to different records; use the IDs returned by the corresponding read rather than substituting an account ID. Catalog membership does not establish rights ownership. The implementation also accepts plan_catalog_members, which is intentionally omitted from this preview request union pending a provider-neutral public module contract. This is a remaining documentation and API design gap, not an access restriction.

### Release verification and review

`verify_release` and `verify_release_tracks` enqueue enabled verification workflows (202); disabled features or unmet readiness conditions return 409. `list_release_tracks`, `read_release_track_observations`, and `review_release_track_identities` inspect saved slots and identity evidence (200). Inspect the returned readiness, coverage and unresolved identity state before using a recording match. `list_release_cases`, `read_release_case`, `read_release_case_review`, and `review_release_case` read or record release-case review. A review requires the current fingerprint, a decision, and an idempotency key; it does not silently rewrite source evidence.

### Compile and save briefs

`brief` compiles evidence from up to ten completed or partial requests in one workspace without provider or model calls. Purposes are `creative_direction`, `playlist_pitch`, and `company_onboarding`. Creative direction prioritizes lyrics and artwork; playlist pitching prioritizes catalog/audio metadata. Inspect readiness, request_coverage, selected input versions and gaps. Briefs are evidence packets, not finished creative concepts or outreach. `save_brief` freezes the server-compiled output, and `read_brief` retrieves that snapshot without recompilation. Newer evidence can supersede a snapshot without rewriting it; withdrawn evidence or removed scope can withhold its payload. All three actions return 200.

### Link retained evidence

`attach_evidence` links one exact retained `source_version_id` to 1–100 distinct existing targets: an artist, a professional, or a Context request/subject pair. Supply a stable `idempotency_key`; retry only the same version and targets with that key. Authentication supplies the actor. The receipt records relevance only; it does not confirm identity, rights or a business mandate. It creates no roster entry and makes no provider/model call or charge.

`read_evidence_attachment` reads one receipt by `attachment_id`. `list_evidence_attachments` reads a page for an exact source version. Pass `next_id` as `after_id` while `has_more` is true, including an empty page where protected receipts were withheld. Reads check current workspace access, source retention and independent target access. A later source version needs a separate association; these actions do not rewrite historical receipts. They require the matching evidence-association database and API release; accepted request syntax is not hosted availability.

### Scope and failures

Authentication determines the account. Optional organization_id selects an authorized organization workspace; request and subject ownership are checked again by the operation. Invalid request syntax returns 400, missing authentication 401, rejected organization access 403, and operation conflicts, unavailable evidence or disabled verification 409. No action accepts a caller-supplied account identity. Local schema tests do not establish hosted availability.

### MCP mapping

Standard MCP uses the `context` tool with the same action and fields as this REST request. The three evidence actions also have individually discoverable object-schema tools listed separately below; they are excluded from delegated OAuth connections. Delegated OAuth exposes the named tools below and supplies the action server-side; omit action from the named tool input. These registrations require the full `mcp:tools` grant, current ownership and fresh credential verification. Read-only is a tool annotation, not a guarantee of hosted readiness. Discover the actual tools in the connected client before use; this is a static source mapping, not a verified client catalog. The omitted provider-bound planning action is still a remaining contract gap.

attachEvidence.summary: Link an already-retained synthetic version to an existing authorized artist

202.description: Accepted ingest, verify_release, or verify_release_tracks. Ingest returns request; verification returns request_id and verificationQueued, or request_id, subject_id and lookupQueued. Acceptance does not mean completion.

200.description:
Action-specific result: request, page, execution(s), observation, review, saved snapshot, release-case result, module plan, or a compiled brief. Inspect readiness and coverage; 200 does not establish complete evidence.

Read returns request. Brief returns request_id, request_ids, purpose, readiness, bounded Markdown text and text_characters, documents and their serialized characters count, missingTopics, guidance, gaps, request_coverage, and input_manifest. Each coverage entry includes requestId, readiness and missingTopics; overall readiness remains partial if any request has a gap or partial evidence. The manifest includes compilerVersion, method, requestIds, excludedTopics, and selected documents with documentId, resultId (null when not recorded), subjectId, topic, version and sourceVersionIds. The result is returned without creating a saved brief record. Save/read brief return {snapshot: {id, created_at, purpose, state, superseded, brief}}. state is saved or unavailable; unavailable snapshots return brief: null. saved snapshots return the exact compiled response including its input manifest. Another workspace cannot read the record. Company-onboarding briefs also include assessment_scope and next_steps. Other action groups return the action-specific result described above; a successful response does not establish complete coverage.

Attach/read evidence returns a ContextEvidenceAttachmentReceipt: receipt, owner, original actor and exact source-version IDs, creation time, typed targets, assertion `relevance_only`, `rights_verified: false`, and policy version. List evidence returns ContextEvidenceAttachmentPage with `items` (up to 50 receipts), `next_id` and `has_more`. Continue with the cursor even when a page has no visible receipts. Scope/retention failures reveal no protected receipt.

409.description: Operation failed, access unavailable, input/key conflict, or request not found. Retry ingestion with the same idempotency key after correcting the cause.

403.description: The authenticated account cannot access the selected organization workspace.

post.description: Feature-flagged metadata pilot. Saves a Spotify track URL in a temporary workspace before signup. Uses an HttpOnly seven-day cookie; only its hash is stored. One URL per guest session and 100 new guest workspaces per day globally. Extracts artist and release metadata only. Does not run paid enrichment, generate a site, or send email. Serve through the same-origin funnel; cross-site cookie integration is not provided. Retry the same URL and cookie to resume dispatch.

post.description: Requires the original guest cookie plus verified account authentication. Optionally claims into an authorized organization. Transfers saved metadata without refetching it; an in-progress worker finishes into the claimed destination. Repeated claims by the same account and destination return the same request ID. Another account cannot claim it. Existing matching identities and customer corrections are preserved. No artist ownership claim is implied. Signup UI integration must call this endpoint after authentication. The Recoup app provides a /context entry page and claims into the personal account after login. A failed extraction remains retryable through the same claim receipt. No completion email or website is generated by this flow.
